full_text_en:
Longquan County Sword Factory v. Longquan County Wan Zihao Sword Factory — dispute over infringement of trademark right

Plaintiff: Zhejiang Province Longquan County Sword Factory (hereinafter referred to as County Sword Factory).

Legal Representative: Zhao Shuiquan, Director of Longquan County Sword Factory.

Agent ad litem: Shi Shujin, Chen Shuming, lawyers from Lishui Prefecture Law Firm.

Defendant: Zhejiang Province Longquan County Wan Zihao Sword Factory (hereinafter referred to as Wan Zihao Sword Factory).

Legal Representative: Wang Zhenming, Director of Longquan County Wan Zihao Sword Factory.

Agent ad litem: Mao Huiqing, Zhang Guoping, lawyers from Hangzhou No. 2 Law Firm.

In the case of the plaintiff County Sword Factory v. the defendant Wan Zihao Sword Factory regarding a dispute over infringement of trademark right, the Lishui Intermediate People's Court accepted the case and, in accordance with the law, formed a collegial panel. After a public hearing on November 19, 1987, the court found that:

Since its establishment in 1956, the plaintiff County Sword Factory has used the trademarks "Longquan" and "Longfeng Qixing" on the swords it produced. In February 1979, the plaintiff applied to register the "Longquan" trademark. On October 31 of the same year, the State Administration for Industry and Commerce approved the registration of the "Longquan" trademark, with Registration Certificate No. 130250. The trademark consists of the four characters "Longquan Baodao" (龙泉宝剑) in vertical, seal-script, traditional Chinese characters. In May 1984, the plaintiff further applied to register the "Longfeng Qixing" trademark, with an accompanying illustration describing: "The front of the sword bears the seal-script characters 'Longquan Baodao' and patterns of a phoenix and seven stars; the back of the sword bears patterns of a dragon and seven stars arranged in the shape of the Big Dipper constellation." On December 30 of the same year, the State Trademark Office approved the registration, with Registration Certificate No. 21813. Thus, the plaintiff obtained the registration certificates for the "Longquan" and "Longfeng Qixing" trademarks, enjoyed the exclusive right to use both trademarks, and could use both trademarks on the same sword blade.

The defendant Wan Zihao Sword Factory, after being approved to commence operations in April 1984, produced swords without its own trademark and instead used the "Longquan" and "Longfeng Qixing" trademarks without authorization. In July 1984, the defendant applied for the "Wan" character trademark, which was approved for registration by the State Trademark Office on March 30, 1985, with Registration Certificate No. 222720. After obtaining the exclusive right to the "Wan" trademark, the defendant used the "Wan" trademark on the swords it produced, but at the same time also used the plaintiff's registered "Longquan" and "Longfeng Qixing" trademarks on the same sword blades. In response, in January 1985, the plaintiff filed a complaint with the Longquan County Administration for Industry and Commerce, requesting an order to cease the defendant's infringing acts. The Longquan County Administration for Industry and Commerce convened a meeting of relevant sword factories and clearly stated: "Longquan" and "Longfeng Qixing" are registered trademarks of the County Sword Factory, and other factories must enter into a licensing agreement with the registrant before they can use them. After this, the defendant changed the trademarks on the swords it produced to "Longquan Gujian" (Ancient Longquan Sword), "Longfeng Qijing" (Dragon and Phoenix Seven Wells), "Shuanglong Qijing" (Double Dragon Seven Wells), and "Shuangfeng Qijing" (Double Phoenix Seven Wells), but the packaging still used the four characters "Longquan Baodao" (龙泉宝剑), with the font arrangement identical to that of the plaintiff's registered trademark. The product instructions also contained content such as "Longquan Baodao" and "Longfeng Qixing." To protect its trademark rights, the plaintiff filed a lawsuit with the Lishui Intermediate People's Court on September 4, 1987, requesting that the defendant cease the infringing acts and compensate for the profits obtained from the infringement, amounting to RMB 205,000. The defendant admitted in its defense that it had formally infringed upon the plaintiff's registered trademark rights but argued that the amount of compensation was unreasonable.

During the trial of this case, the Lishui Intermediate People's Court, on September 24 and October 21, 1987, in accordance with Article 93, Paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (for Trial Implementation), issued rulings ordering the defendant to immediately cease using trademarks identical or similar to the plaintiff's registered trademarks on the same kind of goods, and sealed up 1,735 swords, as well as the packaging and product instructions in inventory. At the same time, the court commissioned the Lishui Prefecture Audit Bureau to determine the profits obtained by the defendant from the production of swords. The audit determined that the defendant had obtained total profits of RMB 96,670.65 from 1984 to August 1987.

The Lishui Intermediate People's Court held at trial: Article 3 of the Trademark Law of the PRC provides: "Trademarks approved and registered by the Trademark Office are registered trademarks, and the registrant of a trademark enjoys the exclusive right to use the trademark, which is protected by law." The plaintiff lawfully enjoys the exclusive right to use the registered trademarks "Longquan" brand and "Longfeng Qixing" brand for swords. Without the permission of the registered trademark owner, the defendant used on the same kind of goods the wording "Longquan Baodao" (龙泉宝剑) and "Longquan Gujian" (龙泉古剑) identical or similar to the plaintiff's registered trademarks, as well as the patterns of "Longfeng Qixing," "Shuanglong Qijing," and "Shuangfeng Qijing," which violated Article 38, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph (1) of the Trademark Law and infringed upon the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its registered trademarks. On the basis of ascertaining the facts and clarifying the liability, the court convened mediation between the parties, but no agreement was reached. Accordingly, on November 23, 1987, the Lishui Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment:

1. The defendant shall immediately cease using trademarks identical or similar to the plaintiff's registered trademarks on the swords it produces (including packaging and instructions);

2. The defendant shall remove from its existing swords and packaging all trademark identifiers that are identical or similar to the plaintiff's registered trademarks, and destroy all existing product instructions;

3. The defendant shall fully compensate the plaintiff for the profits obtained from the infringement during the period of infringement, amounting to RMB 96,670.65, to be paid within three months after the judgment takes effect.

The litigation costs for this case amount to RMB 1,450, and the appraisal costs amount to RMB 416, all to be borne by the defendant.

After the judgment of the first instance was announced, the defendant appealed to the Zhejiang High People's Court, claiming that the original appraisal had failed to include certain expenses as production costs, and requested a review of the original appraisal.

After accepting the appellant's appeal, the Zhejiang High People's Court entrusted the original appraisal authority to review the conclusion regarding the profits from the sale of infringing products by the Wan Zihao Sword Factory. During the review, the Wan Zihao Sword Factory provided some documents that should have been entered into the accounts but were not. Accordingly, the Lishui Prefecture Audit Bureau lawfully made a new appraisal: the profits from the sale of infringing products by the Wan Zihao Sword Factory amounted to RMB 91,505.15, which included income tax already paid of RMB 47,047 and tax reductions and exemptions granted by the state of RMB 7,370.01.

The Zhejiang High People's Court held at trial: The respondent lawfully obtained the exclusive right to use the registered trademarks "Longquan" and "Longfeng Qixing" in October 1979 and December 1984, respectively. Without the permission of the registered trademark owner, the appellant used trademarks identical to the respondent's registered "Longquan" and "Longfeng Qixing" trademarks on the swords it produced, constituting an infringement of the exclusive right to use the registered trademark; the use of trademarks similar to "Longquan" and "Longfeng Qixing" on the "Longquan Gujian," "Shuanglong Qijing," and "Shuangfeng Qijing" swords, as well as on packaging and product instructions, also constituted infringement. The original trial court's judgment was accurate in characterization and the trial procedure was lawful. The fault for the miscalculation of the profit amount from product sales during the infringement period by the appraisal authority lies with the appellant, who failed to provide evidence in accordance with the law during the trial in the original court.

After mediation by the Zhejiang High People's Court proved ineffective, in accordance with Article 151, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (for Trial Implementation), the court rendered the following judgment on March 30, 1988:

1. Affirm Items 1 and 2 of the judgment of the Lishui Intermediate People's Court;

2. Amend Item 3 as follows: the Wan Zihao Sword Factory shall fully compensate the County Sword Factory for the profits obtained from the infringement during the period of infringement, amounting to RMB 37,088.14, to be paid within ten days after service of this judgment;

3. The tax reductions and exemptions granted by the state to the Wan Zihao Sword Factory during the infringement period, amounting to RMB 7,370.01, shall be turned over to the State Treasury.

The litigation costs for this appeal amount to RMB 1,450, and the appraisal costs amount to RMB 500, all to be borne by the Wan Zihao Sword Factory.
